issues.description: The architecture lets unconstrained residual heads compensate for weak physics branches, so aggregate accuracy can improve while component fidelity degrades.
issues.original_snippet: Architecture: shared Transformer encoder + FiLM-conditioned physics branches (PV, Wind, Battery) + behavioral Load branch (Temp MLP + GRU temporal module) + per-component residual heads.
issues.suggested_fix: Constrain residuals as bounded corrections after physically valid component predictions, add residual magnitude or orthogonality penalties, and select checkpoints with component-level constraints in addition to aggregate loss.
issues.rationale: A residual bypass can learn the target directly and hide errors in PV, wind, load, or battery branches, which undermines the stated physics-informed decomposition.

issues.description: The curriculum reduces component supervision after epoch 8 even though the best checkpoints occur around epochs 4-9.
issues.original_snippet: 2-phase curriculum (Phase1 epochs 1-8: component_loss_weight=0.03, Phase2 epochs 9+: cw=0.02).
issues.suggested_fix: Use normalized per-component losses with adaptive weighting, or pretrain theory branches before enabling residual heads instead of lowering component pressure near convergence.
issues.rationale: Lowering the component loss when the model is already settling can encourage the aggregate objective and residual heads to dominate the physical branches.

issues.description: The balance-point load model is instantaneous and omits thermal inertia, lagged temperature exposure, humidity, calendar effects, and occupancy-like structure.
issues.original_snippet: load_temp = α_h * softplus(T_bal_h − T) + α_c * softplus(T − T_bal_c)
issues.suggested_fix: Use lagged temperature states or degree-hour features, optionally with a small constrained correction network over temperature history and calendar context.
issues.rationale: Building load typically responds to accumulated thermal state rather than only current temperature, so a static curve is likely misspecified.

issues.description: Plain softplus produces nonzero heating or cooling contribution at the balance point, which biases the physical interpretation of the setpoints.
issues.original_snippet: load_temp = α_h * softplus(T_bal_h − T) + α_c * softplus(T − T_bal_c)
issues.suggested_fix: Use shifted smooth hinges such as softplus(kx)/k - softplus(0)/k with learnable or fixed sharpness, or a constrained piecewise-linear deadband model.
issues.rationale: At x=0, softplus is positive, so the model does not represent zero heating or cooling demand at the learned threshold without relying on a compensating offset.

issues.description: The heating and cooling balance points are independent, so the learned model can collapse or invert the deadband.
issues.original_snippet: Parameters: T_bal_h (init 18°C), T_bal_c (init 24°C), α_heat_raw, α_cool_raw (softplus positive), base_offset.
issues.suggested_fix: Parameterize T_bal_c = T_bal_h + min_gap + softplus(delta_gap), and regularize setpoints to plausible HVAC ranges.
issues.rationale: Without an ordering constraint, optimization can create overlapping heating and cooling regimes that are physically hard to justify.

issues.description: The design declares a base_offset parameter that is absent from the displayed load_temp equation.
issues.original_snippet: Parameters: T_bal_h (init 18°C), T_bal_c (init 24°C), α_heat_raw, α_cool_raw (softplus positive), base_offset.
issues.suggested_fix: Either include + base_offset in the formal model and test it, or remove the parameter from the implementation and documentation.
issues.rationale: A mismatch between the mathematical spec and parameter list creates risk of a dead parameter or an undocumented bias term.

issues.description: The aggregate MAE hides severe component degradation, especially for V7 BP across load, PV, wind, battery power, and SOC.
issues.suggested_fix: Promote component metrics to gating criteria, report Pareto tradeoffs, and require physically valid component decomposition before accepting equal net-power accuracy.
issues.rationale: For VPP forecasting, a model that gets net power right through cancellation can still be physically wrong and operationally unsafe.

issues.description: Residual Mean is being interpreted as residual correction size even though V7 BP has much higher residual variance.
issues.suggested_fix: Report residual MAE, RMSE, signed bias, variance, autocorrelation, and per-component residual energy before concluding that correction is smaller.
issues.rationale: A near-zero mean can simply indicate unbiased corrections, while the residual head may still be doing more work through larger positive and negative swings.

issues.description: Battery power and SOC errors suggest the design lacks a hard battery state-transition mechanism.
issues.suggested_fix: Model SOC with a differentiable state update using charge/discharge efficiency, capacity, bounds, and ramp constraints, and penalize or project invalid trajectories.
issues.rationale: SOC is a cumulative state, so predicting it as another loose branch output can violate energy conservation and amplify small battery-power errors over time.

issues.description: The learning-rate schedule is misaligned with observed convergence because the first restart happens long after all best checkpoints.
issues.original_snippet:
ALL 4 experiments converge to best Val MSE between epochs 4-9. NO experiment improves after epoch 14.

The CosineAnnealingWarmRestarts at epoch 25 gave a transient Val MSE dip ... but could not beat the early best.
issues.suggested_fix: Run an LR-range test and compare shorter schedules such as one-cycle over 8-12 epochs, flat-then-decay, or cosine with T_0 shorter than the observed convergence window.
issues.rationale: A restart at epoch 25 cannot address optimization dynamics that have already plateaued by epoch 14.

issues.description: Validation MSE values are on a very different scale from final test MSE, but the design does not define the metric transform or units.
issues.original_snippet:
| Config | Best Epoch | Best Val MSE | Best post-epoch-14 |
| V6 S2 gru64 | 9 | 0.386476 | 0.422546 (ep15) |
| V7 BP | 4 | 0.427316 | 0.430146 (ep27) |
issues.suggested_fix: Report whether validation MSE is normalized, scaled, or composite, and include raw-unit validation metrics comparable to the test table.
issues.rationale: Without metric-scale clarity, conclusions about convergence, checkpoint quality, and schedule effectiveness are hard to audit.

issues.description: The early-stopping configuration wastes most of the training budget after the useful convergence window.
issues.original_snippet: All experiments early-stopped at epoch 39 (patience=20, start_epoch=20).
issues.suggested_fix: Start early stopping shortly after warmup, use patience around 5-8 with min_delta, and cap this ablation family near 15 epochs unless later improvements are demonstrated.
issues.rationale: If no run improves after epoch 14, continuing to epoch 39 consumes roughly two thirds of compute without improving model selection.

issues.description: The previous V6.1 baseline is treated as comparable even though its metrics differ materially from the current V6 S2 baseline.
issues.original_snippet:
V6.1 2x2 ablation (N29: remove temp from GRU, N30: selective gradient detach) on same base architecture:

| baseline | 0.001952 | 7.691e-06 | 0.002483 | -0.000949 |
issues.suggested_fix: Rerun the gradient-isolation ablation under the exact current code, data split, seed protocol, and metric pipeline, then report confidence intervals.
issues.rationale: Cross-run baseline drift can make the apparent benefit of detach or temperature changes look larger or smaller than it really is.

issues.description: Binary gradient detach is a blunt isolation mechanism that can improve theory metrics while starving the shared encoder or hurting aggregate accuracy.
issues.original_snippet: V6.1 detach (N30) achieved Theory MAE -10% vs baseline ... by selectively detaching residual-head gradients from load/PV/wind theory branches. But V6.1 full (N29+N30) was antagonistic — too much isolation starved the encoder.
issues.suggested_fix: Replace binary detach with gradient scaling, PCGrad/GradNorm-style conflict handling, or staged residual unfreezing, and evaluate with multi-seed paired runs.
issues.rationale: The reported antagonism is exactly the failure mode expected when shared representations receive incomplete or conflicting gradients.
